mainTopic: Shed wool from an עולה and dangling wool, the end of פרק הלוקח בהמה, and the new משנה on how long an owner cares for a בכור before giving it to a כהן.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question: does the רבנן's ban on wool shed from a בכור also apply to an עולה? The גמרא tries to answer from a ברייתא about plucked wool. That proof is pushed away, because the word 'plucks' may have been chosen only to show how far עקביא goes. Next the גמרא defines dangling wool that 'does not appear with the fleece'. ריש לקיש and רב נתן בר אושעיא give two different tests, and רבי אילעא explains ריש לקיש's view. Then פרק הלוקח בהמה ends, and a new משנה teaches how long an owner must care for a בכור, and how long it may be kept before it is eaten. The גמרא looks for the source of the 30 and 50 days. רב כהנא's pairing of פסוקים is shown to be reversible, so רבא learns the extra time for an ox from the word 'תעשה', and the exact number is left to the חכמים. Finally רב ששת explains why the owner may not hand the בכור over early. A ברייתא forbids giving priestly gifts as wages, and that ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Should the shed-wool rule apply to a burnt offering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking whether wool shed from an עולה is forbidden, giving a reason for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that because an עולה's main job is not כפרה, a person might hold on to it, so the rule applies? Or do we say that because an עולה also brings כפרה for a missed מצות עשה, a person would not hold on to it, so the rule does not apply?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a question about an עולה. It asks whether the rule against using wool that fell off a בכור should also apply to an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about the בכור exists because an owner might delay slaughtering it in order to collect wool. The question is whether an owner would also delay an עולה. One side says yes, since its main purpose is not כפרה. The other side says no, since it still brings כפרה for a missed מצות עשה, and people want their כפרה quickly.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
He keeps it around and delays offering it
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: This text starts in the middle of a sentence. The words just before it ask about wool that fell off an עולה. The phrase 'its main purpose is not כפרה' is describing the עולה.

phrases.english: since its main purpose is not to come for atonement
phrases.notes: 'Its' is the עולה from the question just before this.

phrases.english: one might keep it around (and delay offering it)
or perhaps
since a burnt offering also atones for a positive commandment
one would not keep it around?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a question the גמרא began just before this text.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the גזירה against shed wool also apply to an עולה, or only to a בכור?

steps.title: Proof from a teaching about plucking wool from a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids wool that someone plucked from a בכור תם. The גמרא reads this to mean wool that fell out by itself is permitted, and then an עולה would be permitted all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone plucks wool from an unblemished בכור, then even if the animal later gets a blemish and he slaughters it, the wool is forbidden. The reason is only because he plucked it. If it fell out by itself, it is permitted. If so, an עולה, which people do not keep around, is surely permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. It reads the word 'plucks' closely to learn what the law is when wool falls out on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbids plucked wool. That suggests wool that came out on its own is allowed, even from a בכור that people might keep around. If a בכור is allowed, then an עולה, which people do not delay, should certainly be allowed. That reasoning is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source to answer a question)
One who plucks or pulls out
A firstborn animal with no blemish
It was pulled out (by itself, not by a person)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
one who plucks wool from an unblemished firstborn

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנּוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם
phrases.english: even though it later got a blemish
and he slaughtered it, (the wool) is forbidden.
the reason is because he plucked it
but if it came out by itself, it is permitted

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן עוֹלָה דְּלָא מְשַׁהֵי לַהּ!
phrases.english: and all the more so a burnt offering, which one does not keep around!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Wool that comes off an עולה by itself is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about plucking wool from a בכור תם, read to mean that wool that came out by itself is permitted.

steps.title: The word 'plucks' was chosen to show how far עקביא goes
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed away. Wool that came out by itself from a בכור תם is also forbidden. The ברייתא says 'plucks' only because of its second half, where עקביא permits even plucked wool from a בעל מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, wool that came out by itself is also forbidden. The ברייתא says 'plucks' to show how strong עקביא's opinion is. In the case of a blemished animal, he permits the wool even when someone plucked it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the ברייתא. It explains that the word 'plucks' was chosen for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has a second half about a בעל מום, where עקביא permits the wool even when it was plucked. To show how far עקביא goes, the ברייתא uses 'plucks' there, and it keeps the same word in the first half. So we cannot learn from the first half that wool coming out by itself is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (how far-reaching) of his opinion
עקביא בן מהללאל, a תנא who permits this wool

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ נִתְלַשׁ נָמֵי אָסוּר
phrases.english: the same is true: even if it came out by itself, it is also forbidden
and the reason it teaches 'plucks'
is to show you how far עקביא's view goes
that with a blemished animal
even when one plucks it, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין אֲפִילּוּ נִתְלַשׁ נָמֵי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the inference from the word 'plucks'. The ברייתא's ruling itself stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'plucks' was chosen to show how far עקביא goes in the second half, not to exclude wool that came out by itself.

steps.title: But our משנה speaks of shed wool
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that our משנה presents עקביא's view with wool that was shed, not plucked.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in our משנה we learned the case as wool that 'was shed'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 3 using the wording of our own משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said that עקביא permits even plucked wool. But our משנה describes the argument between עקביא and the רבנן using wool that was shed. That seems to suggest the argument is only about shed wool.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in the משנה)...!
It fell out or was shed

phrases.english: But we learned 'was shed' (in our משנה)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that עקביא permits even plucked wool.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה presents the argument with shed wool, which suggests עקביא only permits wool that was shed.

steps.title: Each source shows the strength of a different opinion
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses 'shed' to show how far the רבנן go. The ברייתא uses 'plucks' to show how far עקביא goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught 'was shed' to show how far the רבנן go. The ברייתא taught 'plucks' to show how far עקביא goes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Each source picked its wording to highlight the most extreme form of a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using 'shed' shows that the רבנן forbid the wool even in the easiest case, where no one touched the animal. Using 'plucks' shows that עקביא permits it even in the hardest case, where a person pulled it out. The two sources do not contradict each other, so the rejection in step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How far the רבנן's opinion goes

steps.whatToRemember: A source may choose its wording to show the extreme edge of one opinion. The משנה says 'shed' to show how far the רבנן go, and the ברייתא says 'plucks' to show how far עקביא goes. So the question about an עולה is still not answered by this ברייתא.

phrases.english: It taught 'was shed'
phrases.notes: This is our משנה.

phrases.english: to show you how far the רבנן's view goes
it taught 'plucks'
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא.

phrases.english: to show you how far עקביא's view goes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source's wording has a different purpose.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה says 'shed', the argument is only about wool that was shed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה shows how far the רבנן go, and the ברייתא shows how far עקביא goes. Both wordings stand together.

steps.title: What counts as wool that does not appear with the fleece?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about dangling wool and asks for the exact meaning of 'does not appear with the fleece'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה spoke of dangling wool. What does 'it does not appear with the fleece' mean in practice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line in the משנה about dangling wool and asks a definition question. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says dangling wool that looks like part of the fleece is permitted, and wool that does not is forbidden. The גמרא wants a clear test for which strands 'do not appear with the fleece'.

keyTerms.meaning: Dangling wool, partly loose but still hanging on the animal
What is the case? How do we picture it?
The fleece, the wool sheared off as one piece

phrases.english: Wool that is dangling, etc.
What is the case of 'it does not appear with the fleece'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of shed wool from an עולה and moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A clear test for which dangling strands count as not looking like part of the fleece.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: a strand whose root is flipped outward
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, quoted by רבי אלעזר, says it means a strand whose root is turned upside down, facing toward the top.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of ריש לקיש: it is any strand whose root is turned around toward its top.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer to the definition question. ריש לקיש says only a strand that has flipped over, with its root pointing outward, counts as 'not appearing with the fleece'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a narrow test. Only a strand that is clearly reversed is treated as separate from the fleece, so it is forbidden. A strand that just sticks out but is not flipped still counts as part of the fleece.

keyTerms.meaning: Its root, the base of the strand

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says that Reish Lakish says:
Any strand whose root is overturned toward its top.
phrases.notes: He means the strand flipped over, so its root now faces outward instead of into the skin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the definition question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a strand whose root is reversed toward its top counts as not appearing with the fleece.

steps.title: רב נתן בר אושעיא: a strand that does not press down with the fleece
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אושעיא says it means any strand that does not flatten down together with the rest of the fleece.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אושעיא said: it is any strand that does not get pressed down along with the fleece.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the same question. רב נתן says any strand that sticks up when the fleece is pressed counts as 'not appearing with the fleece'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This test is wider than ריש לקיש's. The strand does not need to be flipped over. It only needs to stand apart when the fleece is pressed down, and then it is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya says:
Any strand that is not pressed down together with the fleece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, wider answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any strand that sticks out and does not flatten with the fleece counts as not appearing with it.

steps.title: Why did ריש לקיש not accept the simpler definition?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש did not explain the משנה the way רב נתן בר אושעיא did.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ריש לקיש, what is his reason for not saying it like רב נתן בר אושעיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why ריש לקיש chose his narrow reading. This sets up רבי אילעא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נתן's reading, 'sticks out from the fleece', seems to match the words 'does not appear with the fleece' more naturally. So the גמרא wants to know what made ריש לקיש choose the flipped-root test instead.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish, what is the reason

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא?
phrases.english: that he did not say like Rav Natan bar Oshaya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two answers and asks why ריש לקיש rejected the simpler one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: ריש לקיש's reason for not using the 'not pressed down' test.

steps.title: רבי אילעא: every fleece has some dangling hairs
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא explains that ריש לקיש holds no fleece is ever free of dangling hairs, so the 'sticks out' test cannot be what the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: ריש לקיש holds that a fleece can never exist without some dangling hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא gives ריש לקיש's reason. Loose, sticking-out hairs are a normal part of every fleece, so they cannot be what the משנה forbids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every strand that sticks out were forbidden, then every fleece would contain forbidden hairs. So ריש לקיש says the משנה must mean something unusual, a strand that is fully flipped over. Normal loose hairs are just part of the fleece.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, this is his view

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש forbids only a strand whose root is flipped outward. רב נתן forbids any strand that sticks out. ריש לקיש rejects רב נתן's test because every fleece has some sticking-out hairs.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a says:
Reish Lakish holds,
because it is impossible for a fleece to be
without dangling hairs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא: קָסָבַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why ריש לקיש did not follow רב נתן בר אושעיא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dangling hairs are always found in a fleece, so plain sticking-out hairs count as part of it. Only a reversed strand is separate.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הלוקח בהמה
steps.stepSummary: The closing line marks the end of פרק הלוקח בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, הלוקח בהמה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula for the פרק. It is not an argument. It only marks that the פרק is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'we will return to you' are said at the end of every פרק, together with the פרק's name. Here the פרק is הלוקח בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a perek

phrases.english: We will return to you, HaLoke'ach Behema.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the last discussion.

steps.title: How long the owner must care for a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says a ישראל must care for a בכור for 30 days if it is a small animal and 50 days if it is a large animal. רבי יוסי says 3 months for a small animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Until when must a ישראל care for a בכור? A small animal, 30 days. A large animal, 50 days. רבי יוסי says: a small animal, 3 months.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It sets how long the owner must look after a firstborn animal before he hands it to a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא gives two time periods, one for small animals like sheep and goats and one for large animals like cattle. רבי יוסי disagrees only about small animals and gives them three months.

keyTerms.meaning: To take care of, to tend
A small animal, like a sheep or goat

phrases.english: MISHNA: Until how long
must an Israelite tend to a firstborn?
With a small animal, thirty days,
and with a large animal, fifty days.
Rabbi Yosei says:
With a small animal, three months.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ עַד כַּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל חַיָּיבִין לִיטַּפֵּל בִּבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner tends a בכור for 30 days if small and 50 days if large. רבי יוסי says 3 months for a small animal.

steps.title: When the כהן asks for the בכור early
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן asks for the בכור during the caring period, the owner should not give it to him. If it has a מום and the כהן wants to eat it, or if it is תמים in the time of the מקדש and he wants to offer it, giving it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן says during that time, 'Give it to me,' the owner should not give it. If it has a מום and the כהן says, 'Give it to me so I can eat it,' it is permitted. And when the מקדש stands, if it is תמים and he says, 'Give it to me and I will offer it,' it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains what the owner should do when a כהן asks for the בכור before the caring period is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is that the owner should not hand it over early. There are two exceptions where the כהן wants to use it right away. One is a בעל מום he wants to eat now. The other is a תמים he wants to offer while the מקדש stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the time period, before the caring days are over
An animal with a blemish, which cannot be offered
Without a blemish, fit to be offered

steps.confusionAlert: 'He should not give it to him' is the basic rule only for a plain request. The two cases right after are exceptions, because there the כהן is going to use the animal right away.
steps.whatToRemember: Normally the owner keeps the בכור for the full period. He may give it early only if the כהן will eat it now (a בעל מום) or offer it now (a תמים, when the מקדש stands).

phrases.english: If the priest said to him within that time:

phrases.aramaic: ״תְּנֵהוּ לִי״ — הֲרֵי זֶה לֹא יִתְּנֶנּוּ לוֹ.
phrases.english: 'Give it to me,' he should not give it to him.
And if it is blemished,
and he said to him, 'Give it to me so I may eat it,' it is permitted.
And at the time of the Temple, if it was unblemished,
and he said to him, 'Give it to me and I will sacrifice it,' it is permitted.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, 'to me', is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן: תְּנֵהוּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the caring period and rules on a כהן's early request.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not give the בכור to a כהן during the caring period. Giving it is permitted if it is a בעל מום he will eat, or a תמים he will offer while the מקדש stands.

steps.title: A firstborn is eaten within its year
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a בכור, whether תם or בעל מום, is eaten within its first year, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn animal is eaten 'year by year,' meaning within its year. This applies whether it is unblemished or blemished, as the Torah says: 'Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps going and gives a new rule. A בכור should be eaten within its first year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שנה בשנה' are read as a time limit: the animal should not be held past its year. The rule covers both a תם, which is eaten as a קרבן, and a בעל מום, which is eaten like regular meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Year by year: within its year

phrases.english: The firstborn is eaten year by year,
phrases.notes: He means it should be eaten within its first year, not kept longer.

phrases.english: whether unblemished or blemished,
as it is stated:
"Before ה׳ your God you shall eat it year by year."
phrases.notes: דברים 15:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a new rule about how long the בכור may be held before it is eaten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור, whether תם or בעל מום, is to be eaten within its first year.

steps.title: How long a blemished firstborn may be kept
steps.stepSummary: If a מום appears within the first year, the owner may keep the animal for the full twelve months. After twelve months, he may keep it only thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a blemish appeared during its first year, he may keep it for the whole twelve months. After twelve months, he may keep it only for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains how the one-year limit works when the animal gets a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מום during the first year does not shorten the time: the owner still has all twelve months. Once the year is over, he gets only a short 30-day window and no more.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep it (not slaughter it yet)

phrases.english: If a blemish developed in it within its year,

phrases.aramaic: רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ כׇּל שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: he may keep it for the entire twelve months.
After twelve months,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְקַיְּימוֹ אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: he may keep it only thirty days.

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור is eaten within its year. A מום during the year still allows the full twelve months. After the year, only thirty days are allowed.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the one-year rule from Step 14 applies to a בכור that gets a מום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a מום during the year, the owner may keep the animal all twelve months. After the year, he may keep it only thirty days.

steps.title: Where do the 30 and 50 days come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the caring periods in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the Torah source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question goes back to Step 12: 30 days for a small animal and 50 days for a large one. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches these numbers.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these matters derived?

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the 30 and 50 days of caring from the start of the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא, asking for the source of the rule in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source for caring for a בכור 30 days (small animal) and 50 days (large animal).

steps.title: Sheep are paired with firstborn sons
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא matches 'your firstborn sons' with 'your sheep.' A firstborn son is redeemed at 30 days, so a sheep gets 30 days too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The verse says, 'The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,' and then, 'So shall you do with your sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא starts answering by linking two parts of the same פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn son is redeemed at 30 days. Since the Torah says 'so shall you do with your sheep,' sheep follow the same 30-day timing. That is the small-animal rule in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
For the verse says:
"The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:28. A firstborn son is redeemed at thirty days.

phrases.english: "So shall you do with your sheep."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:29

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16 for small animals.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A sheep gets 30 days because it is linked to a firstborn son, who is redeemed at 30 days.

steps.title: Oxen are paired with the first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא continues: the first fruits are linked to 50 days, and they are paired with 'your ox,' so an ox gets 50 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And: 'Your full harvest and your juice, you shall not delay,' then, 'So shall you do with your ox.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא finishes his answer with the second pairing, for large animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first fruits are brought from שבועות, 50 days after פסח. Pairing them with 'your ox' gives a large animal 50 days, which matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Your full harvest and your juice (first fruits and gifts of produce)

phrases.english: "Your full harvest and your juice, you shall not delay,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:28. First fruits are brought starting from שבועות, fifty days after פסח.

phrases.english: "So shall you do with your ox."

steps.confusionAlert: Both pairings come from the same two פסוקים. The question is only which phrase goes with which animal. Keep track: the 30-day phrase goes with sheep, and the 50-day phrase goes with oxen.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב כהנא's answer with the large-animal pairing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An ox gets 50 days because it is linked to the first fruits, which are tied to 50 days.

steps.title: Why not reverse the pairings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the ox should be paired with the 30 days and the sheep with the 50 days.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to רב כהנא. The two phrases could just as easily be matched the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing in the פסוק clearly says which phrase belongs to which animal. Swapping them would give an ox 30 days and a sheep 50 days, the opposite of the משנה.

phrases.english: I can reverse it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the way רב כהנא matched the phrases in Steps 17 and 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's matching of firstborn sons with sheep and first fruits with oxen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק does not say which phrase goes with which animal, so the opposite matching is equally possible.

steps.title: Earlier goes with earlier
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: it makes sense to match the earlier phrase with the earlier animal, and the later phrase with the later animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is reasonable to match what comes earlier with what comes earlier, and what comes later with what comes later.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא by matching the phrases in order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק, 'your full harvest' comes first and 'your firstborn sons' comes second. In the next פסוק, 'your ox' comes first and 'your sheep' comes second. Matching first with first and second with second gives exactly רב כהנא's pairings.

phrases.english: It stands to reason
that the earlier one goes with the earlier one,
phrases.notes: 'Your full harvest' is said first, and 'your ox' is listed first.

phrases.english: and the later one with the later one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrases could be matched to the animals either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Matching in order (first with first, second with second) supports רב כהנא's pairing.

steps.title: Maybe closest goes with closest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: it could make even more sense to match the phrases that sit right next to each other. That would reverse the result.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, match the one that is right next to it with the one that is right next to it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the 'in order' answer by offering an equally strong rule that points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Your firstborn sons' sits right next to 'so shall you do with your ox.' Matching neighbors would give an ox 30 days, the opposite of the משנה. So the in-order rule does not settle the question, and רב כהנא's reading is left in doubt.

phrases.english: On the contrary,
the one that is next to it goes with the one that is next to it!
phrases.notes: 'Your firstborn sons' ends one פסוק, and 'your ox' starts the next, so they sit side by side.

steps.whyThisMatters: Two reasonable matching rules point in opposite directions. Because of this, רב כהנא's source is not convincing, and the גמרא will need a different source for the 30 and 50 days.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of Step 20 with an opposite matching rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The 'earlier with earlier' answer, and with it the strength of רב כהנא's derivation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Matching by closeness is just as reasonable as matching by order, and it gives the reverse result.

steps.title: רבא finds the ox's extra time in the word 'you shall do'
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the pairing approach and learns from the word 'תעשה' that the ox gets more care time than the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the פסוק says 'you shall do.' The פסוק is adding another round of 'doing' for your ox.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the pairing of phrases could be flipped, the גמרא gives up on it. רבא brings a fresh source for why the ox gets longer than the sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the word 'תעשה' as adding an extra period of care for the ox, on top of what the sheep gets. This no longer depends on which phrase sits next to which. It only shows that the ox gets more than 30 days; it does not yet give an exact number.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is dropped.
Another act of 'doing,' meaning an extra period of care

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse says "you shall do,"
the verse added for you
another "doing" with your ox.
phrases.notes: He means the ox gets an extra stretch of care time on top of the sheep's 30 days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's pairing derivation, which step 21 showed could be reversed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that an ox gets a longer care period than a sheep?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'תעשה' adds an extra period of care for the ox.

steps.title: Why not sixty days for the ox?
steps.stepSummary: If the ox gets another round of 30 days, the total should be 60, not 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is sixty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא: an extra 'doing' sounds like a second 30 days, which would make 60.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's source shows the ox gets more time, but not how much more. The simplest reading of 'another doing' is a repeat of the same 30 days. That gives 60, which clashes with the known number of 50.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead. This introduces a challenge.

phrases.english: But say: sixty!
phrases.notes: Another 30 days on top of the first 30 would make 60.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exact number that comes out of רבא's source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another 'doing' should mean a repeat of 30 days, for a total of 60 rather than 50.

steps.title: The exact number was left to the Sages
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only says the ox gets more time. The חכמים set the amount at 50.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק handed this over only to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק does not set the exact number of days. The חכמים decided it is 50.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the idea that the ox gets extra time. The size of that extra time was left for the חכמים to fix. So 60 is not forced, and 50 stands.

phrases.english: The verse did not hand you over
except to the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 60-day challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The exact amount was given over to the חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An extra 'doing' means another full 30 days, making 60.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק gives extra time, and the חכמים fixed it at 50 days.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same thing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא makes the same reading of 'תעשה' and also says the number was left to the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches the same: 'Give Me your firstborn sons... so you shall do with your sheep.' You might think the ox is the same. So the פסוק says 'you shall do.' It adds another 'doing' for your ox, and the פסוק handed this over only to the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says just what רבא said, to support him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that the ox might be treated like the sheep. Then it uses 'תעשה' to add more time for the ox. It ends with the same line, that the matter was handed to the חכמים. So both רבא's source and the answer to the 60-day question are backed by a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught so in a ברייתא. This introduces support.

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
"The firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:28

phrases.english: "So you shall do with your sheep" —
phrases.notes: שמות 22:29

phrases.english: I might think the same for your ox too?
The verse teaches: "you shall do" —
the verse added for you
another "doing" with your ox,
the verse handed it over only to the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's derivation and the answer about the חכמים.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading of 'תעשה' and the idea that the number was left to the חכמים

steps.title: The rule: thirty days for small animals, fifty for large
steps.stepSummary: From here the חכמים ruled how long an owner must care for a בכור: 30 days for a small animal, 50 for a large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: how long must Israelites look after a בכור? A small animal, 30 days. A large animal, 50 days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and states the practical rule that comes out of the whole discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small animal, like a sheep or goat, gets the 30 days. A large animal, like an ox, gets 50 days, which is the extra time the חכמים set. 'From here' ties this rule to the reading of the פסוק above.

keyTerms.meaning: To tend, to take care of
A small animal, like a sheep or goat

steps.confusionAlert: דקה here means a small animal, such as a sheep or goat, not something 'thin.' גסה means a large animal, such as an ox.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Until how long are Israelites obligated
to tend to a firstborn?
With a small animal — thirty days,
with a large one — fifty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the practical rule that follows from the ברייתא's reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: An owner cares for a small בכור for 30 days and a large בכור for 50 days.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: three months for a small animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says a small animal needs three months, because caring for it takes a lot of work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: for a small animal, three months, because caring for it takes a lot of work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees about the small animal and gives it a longer care period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion gave a small animal only 30 days. רבי יוסי says three months, because it needs a lot of care before it is ready to be handed to the כהן. This is a dissent only about small animals.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
With a small animal — three months,
because its care is extensive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the 30-day rule for small animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small בכור is cared for three months, because it takes a lot of work to raise.

steps.title: Why small animals are hard to raise
steps.stepSummary: A תנא explains that a small animal needs so much care because its teeth are small.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught: because its teeth are small.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא gives the reason why caring for a small animal takes so much work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small teeth mean the young animal cannot eat most foods by itself. So the owner has to work hard to feed it. This explains רבי יוסי's reason that 'its care is extensive.'
steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: 30 days for a small בכור and 50 for a large one, set by the חכמים from the word 'תעשה.' רבי יוסי says three months for a small animal, because its small teeth make it hard to raise.

phrases.english: It was taught: because its teeth are small.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יוסי's reason that the care is extensive.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small animal is hard to raise because its teeth are small.

steps.title: The owner may not hand the בכור over early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that if the כהן asks for the בכור during the care period, the owner should not give it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן says to the owner during the care period, 'Give it to me,' the owner should not give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה (from step 13) to start discussing it. That line says that during the care period the owner should not give the בכור to a כהן who asks for it. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has finished finding the source for the 30 and 50 days. It now moves to the next line of the same משנה, which says the owner may not hand the בכור over early. The משנה gave no reason, so the גמרא asks for one in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Within the time period (the owner's care period)
A priest, who receives the בכור

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן
phrases.english: If the priest said to him within the time period
phrases.notes: This means the care time set just before: 30 days for a small animal, 50 for a large one.

phrases.english: "Give it to me"
he should not give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמַר לוֹ הַכֹּהֵן בְּתוֹךְ הַזְּמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the next line of the משנה (step 13) and opens a new discussion after the source for the care periods has been settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the care period, the owner may not give the בכור to a כהן who asks for it.

steps.title: Asking the reason for the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the owner may not give the בכור to the כהן early.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the owner can't simply hand the animal over. This question sets up רב ששת's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving the בכור early seems to help everyone, since the כהן gets his gift and the owner saves work. So the גמרא wants to know what is wrong with it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 29.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the owner may not give the בכור to the כהן before the care period ends.

steps.title: רב ששת: It looks like the כהן is being paid
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that taking the בכור early makes the כהן look like one who helps at the threshing floor to earn his gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Because it looks like a כהן who helps out at the threshing floors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the reason. If the כהן takes the animal early, he is saving the owner the work of caring for it, so the בכור looks like payment for a favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Priestly gifts must be given as gifts, not as wages. A כהן who takes over the owner's work looks like a כהן who helps a farmer at his threshing floor so that he will get the תרומה. That appearance of payment is what is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the reason
The threshing floors, where grain is processed and תרומה is given

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Because he looks like a priest
who helps out at the threshing floors.
phrases.notes: He means a כהן who helps the farmer so he'll be given the gifts. That makes the gifts look like a paycheck.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנִּרְאֶה כְּכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Taking the בכור early makes it look like the כהן is being paid for helping, like a כהן who helps at the threshing floor.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no gifts as wages for helpers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids giving תרומה and מעשר as wages to כהנים, לוים or poor people who help out, and calls it desecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: כהנים, לוים and poor people who help at the shepherds' place, at the threshing floors, or at the slaughterhouse may not be given תרומה and מעשר as their wages. If people do so, they have desecrated them. About them the פסוק says 'You have corrupted the covenant of Levi,' and it also says 'Do not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, so that you will not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows the case רב ששת was talking about. Giving holy gifts as payment for help is forbidden and counts as desecrating them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רב ששת's comparison. The 'כהן who helps at the threshing floor' is a known forbidden case. The ברייתא adds לוים, the poor, and other places of work, and it quotes two פסוקים against the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
The tithe, given to a לוי (or to the poor)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule: holy gifts must be given freely and may never be used as payment for work.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The priests, the Levites, and the poor
who help out at the shepherds' place,
and at the threshing floors, and at the slaughterhouse

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נוֹתְנִין לָהֶם תְּרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר בִּשְׂכָרָן
phrases.english: we do not give them terumah and tithe as their wages.
And if they do so, they have desecrated it,
and about them the verse says:
"You have corrupted the covenant of Levi"
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:8

phrases.english: And it says:
"And the holy things of the children of Israel
you shall not desecrate, so that you will not die."
phrases.notes: במדבר 18:32

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא about the 'helping כהן' that רב ששת compared to.
steps.raayaObject: רב ששת's idea that a כהן helping at the threshing floor to get gifts is forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding תרומה and מעשר as wages, with פסוקים from מלאכי and במדבר.

steps.title: Why bring a second פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to add a second פסוק with 'and it says'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the second פסוק adds beyond the first. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק already condemns the practice. So the גמרא wants to know what new point the second פסוק teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it says", which introduces an extra פסוק

phrases.english: What is the reason for "and it says"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the structure of the ברייתא in step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק adds beyond the first.

steps.title: The second פסוק teaches a death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The second פסוק shows that this sin is punishable by death, which the first פסוק does not show.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say there is no death penalty, come and hear: 'Do not desecrate the holy things of the children of Israel, so that you will not die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first פסוק only shows the act is wrong. The second פסוק adds that it carries a death penalty from Heaven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first פסוק alone you might think it is a sin with no death penalty. The words 'so that you will not die' in the second פסוק show that it does carry death. That is why both are quoted.

phrases.english: And if you would say: there is no death penalty
come and hear:
"And the holy things of the children of Israel
you shall not desecrate, so that you will not die."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מִיתָה לָא תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first פסוק shows the act is forbidden. The second adds that it is punishable by death.

steps.title: The חכמים wanted to fine the owners
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the חכמים wanted to fine those who paid with gifts by making them separate תרומה again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים wanted to penalize them, and to have them separate a complete תרומה over again for that produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells us the חכמים considered a fine for owners who used תרומה as wages. They would have to separate תרומה a second time, so they would gain nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner who paid his helper with תרומה saved himself money. The proposed fine would take away that gain by making him give תרומה again from his own produce. The next steps explain why this fine was never actually made.

phrases.english: And the Sages wanted to penalize them,
and to have them separate a complete terumah over again for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 32.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים considered fining owners who paid with gifts by making them separate תרומה again.

steps.title: Why was the fine not made?
steps.stepSummary: The text asks why the חכמים did not actually fine them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why did they not penalize them?
steps.whatsHappening: The text asks why the proposed fine was dropped. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine seems fair and would stop the practice. So there must be a reason the חכמים held back.

phrases.english: And for what reason did they not penalize them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the fine of step 35 was not made.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the חכמים did not carry out the fine.

steps.title: The fear of tithing from exempt produce
steps.stepSummary: A second separation might make people think the produce is still untithed, so they would use exempt produce to tithe for obligated produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he will come to separate from exempt produce for obligated produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the fine could cause a new mistake. Seeing תרומה taken a second time, people might think the produce was never properly tithed and use it to tithe other food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law the first separation worked, so the produce is already exempt. Separating תרומה from exempt produce for produce that still needs it does not work, and the other produce would stay untithed. To avoid that mistake, the חכמים gave up the fine.
steps.whatToRemember: Giving תרומה or מעשר as wages for help is forbidden and desecrates them, and it carries a death penalty from Heaven. Still, the חכמים did not fine the owners, because a second separation could lead people to tithe from exempt produce for obligated produce.
steps.confusionAlert: The original separation did work. The fine was not dropped because the first תרומה was invalid, but because a second separation might make people think it was.

phrases.english: Perhaps he will come to separate
from exempt produce for obligated produce.
phrases.notes: Seeing it tithed a second time, someone might think it's still untithed and use it to tithe other food. That wouldn't work.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּלְמָא אָתֵי לְאַפְרוֹשֵׁי מִן הַפְּטוּר עַל הַחִיּוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second separation might lead people to tithe from exempt produce on behalf of obligated produce.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins a rule that covers all its cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא starts a new statement saying that something applies to all of the cases it listed. The rest of the statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in all of them there is in them...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is setting up its next point. It opens with the words "in all of them," and the actual rule comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the ברייתא gave a פסוק for this sin and explained why the חכמים chose not to fine people. Now it widens the view: whatever comes next applies to every case it mentioned, not just one. Wait for the next words before deciding what the rule is.

keyTerms.meaning: And in all of them, meaning all the cases listed in the ברייתא
There is in them; it applies to them. An opening phrase that leads into a rule

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not complete. Do not try to guess the rule from these three words. The ברייתא finishes the sentence on the next amud.

phrases.english: And in all of them there is in them
phrases.notes: "All of them" means every case the ברייתא listed. The sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanation of why the חכמים did not fine them (Step 37), the ברייתא goes on to a rule that covers all the cases it listed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא begins a rule that applies to all of its listed cases. The content of the rule follows on the next amud.
